findings.title: Migration crashes unless embed_category exactly matches a category name
findings.body: The migration always runs execute(SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category')[0]['id']. Site settings are written to the database only when they differ from the YAML default, and embed_category defaults to an empty string, so on a normal install that query returns no rows. [0] is nil and ['id'] raises NoMethodError, rolling the migration back. The later if category_id == 0 fallback never runs in that case, so it does not cover sites that never set embed_category or whose value is not an exact categories.name match (different case, whitespace, slug instead of name). The uncategorized lookup on line 15 has the same [0] crash if that setting row is absent. Production deploys and test DB setup fail before any hosts are copied.

findings.title: Host import interpolates SQL, skips normalization, then deletes the old settings
findings.body: Each legacy host is inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A single quote or backslash in the old embeddable_hosts value is a SQL syntax error that aborts the upgrade, or arbitrary SQL run as the migration database role. The insert also skips EmbeddableHost before_validation, so values the previous allow-check accepted are stored raw. SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? stripped an http:// or https:// prefix and compared the rest to URI#host; a stored value like http://eviltrout.com will not equal URI#host eviltrout.com, so those hosts stop being allowed after upgrade. split on newline also keeps a trailing carriage return and surrounding whitespace, and a line longer than the new varchar(255) host column fails the INSERT. Line 31 then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category rows unconditionally. The migration uses change plus execute, so it is irreversible and rollback cannot restore the deleted settings.

findings.title: Allow-check ignores host case and port
findings.body: record_for_host binds URI#host and queries lower(host) = ? without downcasing the bound value. URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed URL such as http://Example.com/post does not match a stored host of any case, host_allowed? is false, the comments iframe is rejected, and TopicRetriever skips import so the embed stays on the loading view. URI#host also drops the port, but the format validator allows a :port suffix and before_validation does not remove it, so a saved host example.com:8080 is compared to example.com and never matches. An admin can save a port-qualified host that can never embed or import topics, with no error at save time. Downcase the lookup host and compare a canonical form (include a non-default port on both sides, or strip it both when saving and when checking).

findings.title: Host format rejects valid hostnames
findings.body: The format regex requires the final label to be 2 to 5 letters. That rejects hosts an admin needs to allow: gTLDs and older long TLDs such as example.photography or example.museum, IP addresses such as 127.0.0.1, and localhost. Create and update fail validation, so those sites cannot be added, host_allowed? stays false, and their embeds are denied. The same pattern accepts a port and a path, which record_for_host does not treat as the matched host, so the string that can be saved is not the string that is compared. Accept real hostnames and IP addresses, and canonicalize before validating.

findings.title: Nil host crashes in before_validation
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no nil check. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is omitted, and any EmbeddableHost.create/save with a nil host hits the same callback. NoMethodError is raised before format validation, so the request returns 500 instead of a 422. Guard the callback and validate presence so a missing host is a normal validation error.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts make embed category assignment non-deterministic
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation, and the new table has no unique index on host. record_for_host uses an unordered .first after a case-insensitive column comparison, so two rows for the same host, including case variants such as Example.com and example.com which both pass the format check, cause TopicEmbed.import to file new topics in an arbitrary category. The migration can also insert duplicate lines from the old setting. Normalize case on save and add a unique index on lower(host).

findings.title: Missing host update or destroy returns 500
findings.body: update and destroy load the row with where(id: params[:id]).first and never check for nil. destroy then calls host.destroy, and update calls save_host which assigns host.host, so an unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. save_host also reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] without checking the nested hash, so a body without embeddable_host 500s the same way. The admin delete action has no ajax error handler, so the failure is silent in the UI. Use find so RecordNotFound becomes a 404, and return 400 when the nested parameters are missing.

findings.title: Category is not validated and has no foreign key
findings.body: belongs_to :category does not check that the category exists, and category_id is a required integer with no foreign key. The admin controller copies category_id from params and only substitutes SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when the value is blank, so a nonexistent id is saved, as is -1 if the hidden uncategorized setting was never initialized. Deleting a category leaves embeddable host rows pointing at the old id. TopicEmbed.import passes that id to PostCreator, so embedded topics are created uncategorized or with a dangling category_id, which breaks category topic counts and permission lookups. Validate that the category exists and add a foreign key that restricts or nullifies on delete.

findings.title: Removing embed settings drops the SiteSetting API with no shim
findings.body: embeddable_hosts and embed_category are removed from site settings, and SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? is deleted, with no deprecated wrappers. In-repo callers were updated, but plugins, console scripts, and custom jobs that still call SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, SiteSetting.embed_category, or SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? raise NoMethodError after deploy, including during boot if a plugin touches them at load time. The migration also deletes the stored values, so those callers cannot fall back to the old data. Delegate the old methods to EmbeddableHost for a deprecation period, or external embedding integrations will break on upgrade.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so the suite may still see both definitions, but the files are reversed. A later cleanup that drops or overwrites the misnamed file will remove category fabrication for the whole suite, and anyone editing category_fabricator.rb will not find the category definitions. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: New admin endpoints and the data migration are untested
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert that the class subclasses AdminController. They never request create, update, destroy, or show, so they would not catch a 500 on a missing id, a nil host, an invalid category, or a duplicate host. There is no migration spec, so the embed_category [0] crash and the lossy host import are invisible to CI. EmbeddableHost specs cover scheme and path trimming and a basic allow-check, but not mixed-case URLs, ports, rejected TLDs, or duplicate hosts. Add request specs and a migration example that starts from the old site settings before merging.
